content:
So the bot will (currently) have two functions for yall to work with.  The first (and I imagine less useful one in general) is that it will post the same reoccurring messages in a designated channel at specific times each day.  So if you wanted a clock that goes off at say 6am, noon, 6pm, and midnight, you could have it chime the hour at those times each day.

The second (and likely much more useful one) is you can have it post specific messages at certain date/times.  So if on July 4th 2021, at 7am you wanted a rumor to be spread in a specific channel, you could have that happen.

All times are based on PST.

the format for the messages is as follows:
- first line of entry starts with ">>> ", then the time ('HH:MM' for daily, date+time as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' for one-time),
  then "@", then channel name. Next lines after that will be the sent message, until a next line starting with >>> is found
- you can have discord's clickable mentions in the message text:
  - "@everyone" (without any shenanigans) works as you expect, discordpy handles it automatically
  - "@[text here]" will try to make a mention for a group or a member. Square brackets are mandatory.
    The logic is as follows, the first successful one is used:
    - look for a group/role in the server with the name of exactly what's inside the brackets ("text here")
    - if what's inside the brackets is the numerical user id, the mention to them will be generated from it
    - if what's inside the brackets is a nickname the bot recognizes, the mention to them will be generated
    - otherwise, discord api is called to try to find the member whose nickname or name starts with the text in brackets
  - #[text-here] will make a mention to the channel with the name in square brackets.
(sorry about the @ all... didn't mean to was pasting info)

so in the re-occouring file you might see soemthing like this:

```>>> 15:30 @ some-channel
Hey @[Group Seeking Soup], be in channel #[the-soup-store] at 8 PM for the new event!```

and in the date time file:

```>>> 2021-02-16 20:00 @ chat
@[Worker] if this works correctly only DM's should be ping'd, and it should link to the channel #[dm-chat]```
so as your build your module, think about what automated texts you might want to have appear, when, and where.
it does support multi line, and should support the various discord markups (bold, italic, spoiler, etc).  I dont know if it shows encoded images from links... will have to experiment with that a bit
